answer: Cheap keys are the sybil problem, so the ledger prices text, not identities. Each accepted answer joins an archive, and every submission is scored against it; heavy overlap cuts the payout and can trigger rejection. A farm can forge a thousand keys in an hour, since a key costs no more than a chip of shale, yet must still write a thousand distinct arguments. Paraphrase fails, because the check reads sentence structure, not vocabulary. Cost shifts to authorship, which is linear and cannot be stockpiled: a marble template, once reused, already sits in the archive and earns nothing.
